newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica trade deficit widens, inflation down.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica trade deficit widens, inflation down.

text.p: Jamaica's trade deficit continued to grow in the first 10 months of 1996, but inflation is now nearing single-digit levels, according to figures released by the government Thursday.

The trade gap grew by US$145.9 million, or 14 pct, as of October 1996, from US$1.04 billion to US$1.185 billion. Imports grew by 3.8 pct, to US$2.36 billion, while exports declined by 4.8 pct to US$1.175 billion.
All categories of imports except for capital goods showed increases over the 10 months, while the two key export sectors, bauxite and garments, both recorded declines.

The inflation figures for 1996 stood at 15.8 pct, compared with 25.5 pct in 1995. But inflation for the first nine months of the 1996-97 financial year (April-December) stood at 7.5 pct, or 9.6 pct on an annualized basis.
